references.text: List of materials that the Israelites were to give as offerings for the tabernacle, including gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine linen - the same materials mentioned in Exodus 28:5.
Moses conveys the Lord's command to gather materials for the tabernacle, with the same list of materials: gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
The people bring forward the same materials - blue, purple, and scarlet wool as well as fine linen - as offerings for the sanctuary.
The skilled women spun with their own hands and brought what they had woven from blue, purple, and scarlet wool and fine linen.
Description of how the ephod was made from gold, blue and purple wool, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen - fulfilling the instructions from chapter 28.
The skilled craftsmen made the tabernacle's tent curtains from finely twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet wool with cherubim on them.
Shows the connection between God's command regarding the materials and the faithful execution of the work.
Confirms that the specific making of the ephod followed God's original instructions exactly.
Confirms that the specific design and materials of the belt followed God's command exactly.
Illustrates how the specific decorations on the garment were carried out as commanded.
Summarizes that the work on the garments was completed in full accordance with God's command.
